blocks.title: Class diagram
blocks.text: A class diagram is like a map that shows how things are organized in a system, just as you organize your room. It shows what is in each box and how the boxes are related.

items: Room: the overall space containing everything, like the main structure in a class diagram.
Box: a container within the room, like a class.
Attributes: the items each box holds, such as toys in a ToyBox or books in a BookBox.
Methods: actions a box can perform, such as open or close.
Specific boxes: ToyBox, BookBox and ClothesBox are special kinds of the general Box class.

blocks.text: In Figure 1.10, the Room class (name, size) contains the Box class (label, contents), and the ToyBox (toys), BookBox (books) and ClothesBox (clothes) classes are drawn below it with arrows pointing to Box, showing that they are specialized kinds of box. A class diagram is simply a way to show how the parts of a system work together so that everything can be understood at a glance.

blocks.prompt: In the room example, what plays the part of a class, an attribute and a method?
blocks.explanation: A box is a class; what it holds (its label, its toys, books or clothes) are attributes; what it can do (open, close) are methods.

items: Class diagram: classes with attributes and methods and their relationships, like boxes in a room (Fig. 1.10).
ToyBox, BookBox and ClothesBox are specialized kinds of the general Box class.
